deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is a draft of §21 of Riemann's Inauguraldissertation (1851), the conformal-mapping (Riemann mapping) theorem. The previous page computes the winding-point term in the boundary integral of ∂u/∂p. This page carries out the step 'map a simply connected surface T conformally onto the disc'.

(1) Construction of t. Fix an interior point O_0 (z = z'). Put Θ = log(z − z') = log r + iφ. To make Θ single-valued, cut T along a line from O_0 to the boundary. Crossing this line from its negative to its positive side, Θ changes by −2πi (sign as the manuscript gives it). Riemann seeks an auxiliary function, call it w = α + iβ (my label), with three properties:
- Θ + w is purely imaginary on the boundary, i.e. α = −log r on ∂T.
- w is continuous inside T.
- Any infinitely small change of position changes w only by an amount of the same order.
The garbled formula ∫((∂w/∂x)² + (∂w/∂y)²) is the Dirichlet integral. It vanishes in the part of T where the comparison function coincides with Θ and is finite in the rest. By the Dirichlet-principle theorem of the earlier sections (§§16–18), such a function exists. It is then turned into a single-valued function t = m + ni = log(z − z') + w of z, determined up to a purely imaginary additive constant.

(2) Properties of the real part m:
- m = 0 on the boundary.
- m → −∞ at O_0 (like log r).
- m is harmonic and continuous in the rest of T.

(3) Maximum-principle argument. For a constant a < 0, the set {m < a} is a single connected piece containing O_0.
- A separate piece would have m = a on its border and m < a inside, so m would have an interior minimum. A harmonic function cannot.
- Any region enclosed by {m < a} on which m > a would have m = a on its border and m > a inside, giving an interior maximum. Again impossible.
- Likewise the level line cannot run into the region m > a. Near its points m must increase on one side and decrease on the other.
Hence each level curve m = a is a single closed curve surrounding O_0. Along it, m < a on the inner side, so ∂m/∂p > 0 for the outward normal p. By Cauchy–Riemann (my step), ∂n/∂s = ∂m/∂p > 0, so n increases monotonically along the curve (the manuscript writes 'folglich ∂n/∂s positiv').

(4) Sign of m. m cannot become positive in the interior of T. Since m = 0 on the boundary, a positive value would force an interior maximum, contradicting the principle marked x.

The page breaks off at 'Der imaginäre Theil…'. In the published text this continues: n increases by 2π around each level curve, so e^t maps T one-to-one onto the unit disc.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The sign of the jump of Θ across the cut (−2πi from the negative to the positive side) depends on orientation conventions and is stated without justification.
Existence of w rests on the Dirichlet principle as used in the dissertation. By modern standards this is unjustified (Weierstrass's 1870 critique); it was later rigorized by Hilbert and others.

The level-set argument is heuristic: smoothness of level curves and the absence of critical points of m are tacitly assumed. Since t' ≠ 0 was not yet established, critical points are not excluded at this stage.

results.what: Construction of a function t with Re t = 0 on ∂T and logarithmic pole at O_0 (the complex Green's function), via the Dirichlet principle
results.modern_name: Green's function / Dirichlet principle construction in the proof of the Riemann mapping theorem

results.what: Level sets {m<a} are connected and contain O_0; m<0 inside; ∂n/∂s>0 along level curves
results.modern_name: Maximum/minimum principle for harmonic functions; level curves of the Green's function
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss/Riemann (the maximum principle in this use appears in Riemann 1851)

results.what: Preparation for conformal mapping of a simply connected T onto the disc by e^t

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of §21 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (the Riemann mapping theorem via the Green's function and the maximum principle). Its content is well known and credited to him.

checkable.asserts: Re Θ = log r is harmonic away from z'=0, so m has the right singularity at O_0
For T = unit disc and z0=1/2, the model t = log((z−z0)/(1−z0̄ z)) has Re t = 0 on |z|=1, i.e. the modulus simplifies to 1
The flux of log r through a circle around z' is 2π, matching the total increase of n = arg-part around a level curve

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); m=log(sqrt(x**2+y**2)); n=atan2(y,x); simplify(diff(m,x)-diff(n,y)), simplify(diff(m,y)+diff(n,x))
checkable.asserts: Cauchy–Riemann for t = log z, used to pass from ∂m/∂p > 0 to ∂n/∂s > 0

transcription_corrections: Line 3: '1 f um −2πi' is most likely '[Θ] sich um −2πi ändert'.
'Theil wo m > ist' should read 'Theil wo m > a ist' (the 'a' is omitted in the transcription).
The final line 'x. [?]' appears to read 'x. zuwider'. It completes the footnote marked x: the conclusion contradicts the principle that a harmonic function has no interior maximum or minimum.
'Fortgang' is likely correct, though possibly 'Fortgang/Übergang'. 'wächst[?]' above the integral is uncertain and may be 'erhält'.
'abgerundet[?]' is doubtful; it is probably 'abgesondert' or similar.
